title: Postwatch Sentinel Journal
content:
Quick personal handoff + temporary runbook patches (scratchpad)

Shift summary (00:00–08:00 local)
- Quiet overall; steady traffic on hosted-api (p95 tokens unchanged).
- Two small pager events: degraded embeddings job + transient ServingRuntime OOMs on dedicated pool.
- Applied a short-term mitigation for OOMs: reduced max_batch_size and enabled per-queue soft drop for low-priority customers.
- Verified that fallback routing to smaller model variant worked during the spike (no user-facing 500s).

Incidents handled (short notes)
1) embeddings-worker backpressure (01:17)
   - Symptom: worker queue length jumped from 30 -> 300 after nightly reindex. Redis list length high, rate-limit alarm fired.
   - Immediate action: scaled embeddings-worker horizontally (k8s replica +3) and temporarily throttled reindex job (juked cron in Airflow).
   - Follow-up: add a quota guard on reindex tasks (RW-2145).

2) Dedicated GPU OOM cluster (03:50)
   - Symptom: 2 nodes reported CUDA OOMs for sessions with long-seq (>=8192 tokens). Model variant was gptx-std-30b-fp16.
   - Quickfix: patch runtime config on the pool to set max_seq_length=4096 for new sessions, and enable continuous_kv_cache:false for the session type flagged in logs.
   - Observed: KV cache memory growth correlated strongly with long-chained chat sessions that used function-calling.
   - Next: write a policy to auto-downscale long-seq requests (draft note below).

Temporary runbook additions (to convert into proper PR)
- Emergency OOM mitigation (temp)
  1. identify affected pool: kubectl get pods -l pool=dedicated-gpu-usw2 -o wide
  2. patch configmap: kubectl patch cm runtime-config -p '\"{\\\"data\\\":{\\\"max_seq_length\\\":\\\"4096\\\"}}\"' || use runtime-admin endpoint (POST /admin/config)
  3. restart only the node agent: kubectl rollout restart daemonset/worker-agent -n inference
  4. monitor nvml and dmesg for immediate regressions (watch nvtop / nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY)
  5. open ticket RW-2145 and tag eng-serving-runtime for follow-up

- Short-term routing fallback checklist
  - Ensure model-variant alias exists for small/medium: e.g., gptx-std-30b -> gptx-30b-compact. If missing, add alias in model-catalog UI.
  - Confirm smart-routing policy: fall back to compatible model with same tokenizer and comparable interface.
  - If fallback triggers, increment temporary flag in request metadata for telemetry: X-RW-Fallback: true

Quickplay commands (copied for next shift)
- Check queues: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_ADMIN" https://ops-api.redwood.ai/v1/queues | jq .
- Restart worker pod: kubectl -n inference delete pod <pod-name> --grace-period=30 --wait=false
- Throttle Airflow DAG: airflow pause DAG reindex_embeddings_daily (or run adhoc backoff)

Escalation & communication notes
- When 3+ nodes OOM within 10m -> escalate to eng-serving-runtime on-call and page oncall-lead. Include snapshot: nvml top dump + /var/log/runtime/error.log (last 500 lines).
- For production degraded latency (p99 > 1.5s above baseline for 15m): open incident channel #incident and ping SRE lead + product oncall. Attach traces from Tempo and per-route token cost snapshot.

Observations / heuristics (informal)
- Long-context client sessions (chat w/ functions) are the most common root cause for sudden memory spikes; try to detect by session metadata: function_call_count > 2 and avg_response_tokens > 1200.
- Caching mismatches: when clients pin model versions that don't support ongoing cache formats, KV cache invalidations can cause large transient loads. Consider a cache-compatibility header in the API.
- Redis slowlog often correlates with bulk enqueue; prefer smaller batched pushes during maintenance windows.

Open follow-ups (short TODOs)
- [ ] Draft PR: add reindex job quota/guard in Airflow (owner: Samir)
- [ ] Run a chaos experiment for fallback routing (owner: Riley)
- [ ] Add telemetry for fallback events: X-RW-Fallback metric (owner: Avery)
- [ ] Create persistent runbook section for OOMs with exact nvml dump commands + sample logs

Questions for next shift / notes to self
- Did throttling the reindex fully clear the queue? I left it paused; please confirm resume window.
- If another OOM cluster appears, capture full node snapshot (gcore + nvml) and dump LRUCaches from runtime admin.

Misc scratch ideas (draft language for runbook)
- "If serving runtime memory pressure crosses 85% for >5m, toggle 'compact-mode' on that pool which reduces KV cache retention and forces aggressive prefix batching."
- "Fallback routing should prioritize equivalent-tokenizers and prefer variants with quantized kernels when latency/SLO is breached."

End of notes. Leave this doc as the ephemeral handoff record; will migrate to /shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/runbooks when stable.

Signature: Avery C. (postwatch)
